text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Palestinian minister delivers message to King Hussein from President Yasser Arafat, discusses with Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali efforts to rescue peace process from crisis.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah leaves for Qatar today to discuss bilateral relations, the peace process and strengthening joint Arab work.
- Opposition parties and Islamic Action front study the option of boycotting parliamentary elections.
- Military court to pass judgement on Saturday on Jordanian soldier Ahmed Daqamsa for shooting Israeli schoolgirls.
- Israeli army says soldier who shot Palestinians in Hebron will not be charged because he mentally ill.
- Press and Publications official says there will be no extension of August 15 deadline for newspapers to meet the demands of the amended press law.
- Jordan wins its first gold medal of 1997 Arab Games, in women's discus throwing.
AD-DUSTOUR

- Opposition parties are leaning towards election boycott, Islamist deputy Mohammad Oweida says. Islamic Action Front has delayed a meeting of its main consultative council to discuss the issue so people realise the seriousness of the situation.
- Arab Bank shares rise again on stock market, accounting for 50 percent of Sunday's turnover.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- King Hussein calls for efforts to overcome obstacles facing the Middle East peace process.
- Tarawnah says the peace process is weakened and Jordan doesn't want it to die.
AL-ASWAQ
- Palestinian Authority asks Jordan to intervene in talks with Israel. Majali and Tarawnah invited to Gaza by Arafat.
- Two doctors tell military court Daqamsa is mentally ill.
- Trade Ministry Secretary-General Mohammad Hala'iqa says Jordanian companies are not afraid of the partnership agreement with Europe or membership of the World Trade Organisation.
JORDAN TIMES
- Jordanian businessmen sceptical that Mediterranean business meeting in Amman will lead to any deals.
